props.title: The six rules that make the agent factual

cards.head: Answer from the graph only
cards.body: GraphRAG retrieves the company's subgraph; the agent may not emit a number that isn't a node.

cards.head: Cite source + time
cards.body: Every figure shows where and when it came from. Missing or stale → ‘not available as of…’.

cards.head: Math in code
cards.body: P/E, YoY, margins computed by a tool, never by the model.

cards.head: Verify before answer
cards.body: A freshness/SHACL gate checks the facts; typed tools only; no free web access; no advice.

props.foot: None of these trusts the model. Each one makes it structurally unable to make things up.

props.title: Stale or source-less data fails the load — automatically
lines: LOAD BLOCKED · bad facts never enter
props.caption: the SHACL rules from part one, now guarding every single load
props.foot: This gate is the anti-hallucination kit in code: the agent can only see facts that passed.

props.title: The user asks in English; the ontology keeps the query honest
lines: # user: “what's Infosys P/E and last quarter?”
props.caption: the ontology is the schema that stops the model inventing fields
props.foot: Anyone can ask in plain English — and only valid, grounded queries ever run.

props.title: The factual stock agent in one breath
props.closer: Give the machine only facts that can prove themselves — and it stops guessing.
items: Ontology = meaning: the vocabulary, and the rule that every fact needs a source + time.
Knowledge graph = memory: companies and factors, each fact sourced and timestamped.
Digital twin = live senses: prices kept current (real-time or 15-min), honest about staleness.
Graph engineering = the plumbing: pipelines, the freshness gate, entity resolution, graph ML.
Agentic engineering = the mind: retrieve, reason over five factors, answer with citations.
Anti-hallucination kit: graph-only answers, cited, math in code — and never investment advice.

props.title: Everything you asked to reason over — as graph nodes

cards.head: Earnings & P/E
cards.body: EPS, PAT, and P/E as metric nodes, each linked to the price and result they derive from.

cards.head: Quarterly results
cards.body: Revenue, PAT, margins per quarter, with YoY and QoQ computed and stored.

cards.head: News & roadmap
cards.body: NewsEvent nodes with sentiment; ManagementGuidance extracted from concalls.

props.foot: Five factors, one graph — so the agent can weigh them together, each fact cited.
